title: Tom O'Mara questions New York's fiscal sustainability and CLCPA framework in recent posts
text:
New York State Senator Tom O’Mara questioned the sustainability and affordability of state spending and tax policies in a series of posts published on March 16 and 17, 2026.
In a post dated March 16, O’Mara asked, “Is it affordable and is it sustainable for the citizens of New York State to continue down this road of spending and taxing?” He also linked to his weekly column.
Later that day, O’Mara addressed environmental policy reform by stating, “It’s about reopening the entire (CLCPA) framework from the ground up.”
On March 17, O’Mara marked a holiday with a brief message: “Happy St. Patrick’s Day! “
O’Mara has served as a member of the New York State Senate after three terms in the Assembly for the 137th District. He has participated on several committees including Finance, Energy and Telecommunications, Judiciary, Rules, and others. His background includes legal work for community organizations such as the Chemung County Industrial Development Agency and St. Joseph’s Hospital. Raised in Horseheads, Chemung County, he resides in Big Flats with his family. O’Mara holds a Juris Doctorate from Syracuse University College of Law and a bachelor’s degree from the Catholic University of America. More information about his career can be found on his official website.
